title: Health Issues in Populations
description: Builds direct-service competency for working with high-risk and underserved populations: formerly incarcerated individuals, people with chronic disease, older adults, and communities experiencing trauma. Includes chronic disease basics, medication support, nutrition, weight-inclusive care, and trauma-informed approaches.
notes: Adapted from Calbright College CHW program outline (course 04 / CHW 504), renumbered per CCC convention.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1500-2000 words each, supporting instructor-led sessions and independent study
learning_objectives: Apply trust-building and culturally responsive approaches with high-risk and underserved populations
Support clients with chronic disease basics, medication adherence, nutrition, and weight-inclusive care within CHW scope
Apply trauma-informed principles across CHW services

lessons.title: Serving High-Risk and Underserved Populations
objectives: Apply trust-building and culturally responsive approaches with high-risk and underserved populations
Adapt services for formerly incarcerated individuals, older adults, and communities experiencing trauma

lessons.title: Chronic Disease Basics and Medication Support
objectives: Support clients with chronic disease basics, medication adherence, nutrition, and weight-inclusive care within CHW scope
Teach self-monitoring skills that increase client independence in chronic disease management

lessons.title: Nutrition and Weight-Inclusive Care
objectives: Deliver nutrition education using weight-inclusive, non-judgmental approaches
Choose education materials appropriate to the audience's culture and literacy

lessons.title: Trauma-Informed Approaches
objectives: Apply trauma-informed principles across CHW services
Recognize and respond to trauma responses and emotional cues in client interactions

sequencing_rationale: Course 4 of 6: direct-service competency with high-risk and underserved populations. Population-specific trust and cultural adaptation first, then the health-content lessons (chronic disease and medication support, nutrition and weight-inclusive care), closing with trauma-informed approaches that wrap all services. Scope assumption: health content stays at CHW support scope — education, adherence support, referral — never diagnosis or medical advice; chronic-disease and trauma-informed content knowledge beyond the skills matrix is raised as proposed competencies.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can explain chronic disease basics (diabetes, hypertension, asthma) and common medication-support tasks at CHW scope.
proposed_competencies.rationale: CHW104 lesson 3 teaches disease-specific content knowledge; the skills matrix covers education delivery behavior but not health-content knowledge.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can apply the core principles of trauma-informed care (safety, trustworthiness, choice, collaboration, empowerment) in CHW services.
proposed_competencies.rationale: CHW104 lesson 5 teaches a trauma-informed framework; the matrix covers emotional-cue response but not the framework itself.
